name: United States
pitch: The widest choice of universities anywhere, strong research funding for master's students, and up to three years of post-study work for STEM graduates.
alerts: Consulates check applicants' social-media accounts as part of 2026 screening, so list every handle you have used in the past five years.
Entry restrictions and visa bonds apply to some nationalities under recent presidential proclamations. Read your local US embassy page before you pay any fee.
visa: F-1 student visa
intakes: Fall (Aug/Sep), Spring (Jan), a few in Summer

ielts.note: Most universities also accept TOEFL, Duolingo or PTE.

tuition.ug: US$10,000–35,000 a year at affordable public universities
tuition.pg: US$12,000–30,000 a year; assistantships can waive it

fee: US$185 visa fee + US$350 SEVIS fee. A US$250 Visa Integrity Fee is in the law; ask your embassy whether it is being collected yet.

funds.amt: The first-year cost printed on your I-20 (tuition + living), usually US$25,000–55,000
funds.how: Bank statements, fixed deposits, an education loan sanction letter, or scholarship and assistantship letters. There is no blocked account.
funds.held: No official holding period. Officers expect liquid money with a believable history, so 3–6 months of statements is the safe norm.
funds.solv: Your sponsor (usually a parent) signs an affidavit of support and adds a bank solvency certificate plus income and tax papers. Money for later years should look plausible too.

work.term: 20 hours a week, on campus only. Off-campus work needs CPT or OPT authorisation.
work.post: OPT gives 12 months of work; STEM degrees add 24 more.

spouse.t: Your spouse and children under 21 can get F-2 visas. An F-2 spouse cannot work and can study only part-time. Show extra funds for each dependant on the I-20.

cities: Aircraft manufacturing and engineering internships, plus plenty of campus assistant jobs.
IT, finance and logistics employers; one of the strongest internship markets in the country.
Hospitals, research labs and university departments hire student workers year-round.

housing.tip: University halls are the easiest first-year choice; shared off-campus apartments are cheaper from the second year. Never send a deposit before a live video viewing.

docs: Form I-20 signed by you and the university
DS-160 confirmation page with barcode
SEVIS I-901 fee receipt
Visa interview appointment letter
SAT/ACT or GRE/GMAT scores if your program asks for them
ug: Shortlist 6–8 universities and check each one's SAT/ACT policy; many are test-optional.
Apply 8–12 months ahead through the Common App or the university's own portal with transcripts, an essay and a recommendation.
Send your IELTS score and upload financial documents so the university can issue the I-20.
Pay the SEVIS I-901 fee once the I-20 arrives.
Fill in the DS-160, pay the visa fee and book an interview at the embassy.
Attend the interview with original academic and financial papers. You may enter up to 30 days before classes start.
pg: Shortlist by department and funding; for research degrees, email potential supervisors first.
Sit the GRE or GMAT if the program requires it.
Apply on each graduate portal with a statement of purpose, CV, 2–3 recommendation letters and transcripts (a WES evaluation if asked).
Apply for teaching or research assistantships at the same time; deadlines are often December–February for Fall.
After admission: I-20, SEVIS fee, DS-160 and the visa interview.
On arrival, report to the international student office so your SEVIS record is activated.

sch.t: Most funding comes from the universities themselves: merit awards for bachelor's students, and teaching or research assistantships that waive tuition and pay a stipend for master's and PhD students. Government scholarships are few and competitive.
list: Fully funded master's and PhD study. Apply through the US embassy or Fulbright commission in your own country, usually between February and October of the year before.
Ten months of non-degree study and professional experience for mid-career professionals. Apply through the US embassy.
For women who are not US citizens, for full-time master's or doctoral study. Deadline in mid-November.

name: United Kingdom
pitch: One-year master's degrees, a clear 28-day bank rule, and the Graduate Route for work after you finish.
alerts: The living-cost amount rises on 30 November 2026 to £1,203 a month outside London and £1,570 in London.
The Graduate Route is planned to shorten from 2 years to 18 months for applications from January 2027. Confirm on GOV.UK before you choose an intake.
visa: Student visa (you need a CAS from your university)
intakes: September (main), January, a few in May

ielts.note: Degree-level students can usually use ordinary IELTS Academic; IELTS for UKVI is needed for foundation and pre-sessional courses.

fee: £558 visa fee + £776 a year Immigration Health Surcharge

funds.amt: £1,203 a month outside London or £1,570 in London, for up to 9 months (£10,827 or £14,130), plus any unpaid first-year tuition
funds.how: A bank statement in your name or your parents' names, or a loan letter from a regulated lender.
funds.held: 28 consecutive days. The statement's closing date must fall within 31 days of the day you apply.
funds.solv: The balance must never drop below the required total during the 28 days, even for one day. For a parent's account add your birth certificate and a signed consent letter.

work.term: 20 hours a week in term time, full-time in official vacations.
work.post: Graduate Route: 2 years (3 after a PhD), due to become 18 months from 2027.

spouse.t: Only PhD and research-based postgraduate students, or government-sponsored students, can bring dependants. Bachelor's and taught master's students cannot. Each dependant needs £680 a month (£845 in London) for up to 9 months.

cities: Retail, care homes, call centres and the car-manufacturing supply chain.
Digital and games studios, logistics and care work; among the lowest rents in England.
Finance, legal and health-tech firms, with a large part-time market in hospitality.

housing.tip: Book university halls for the first year as soon as you firm your offer. For private rooms, check the landlord is registered and the deposit goes into a protection scheme.

docs: CAS number from your university
Tuberculosis test certificate from an approved clinic (required for many countries)
ATAS certificate for certain science and engineering master's courses
Parents' consent letter and your birth certificate if you use their funds
Immigration Health Surcharge payment reference
ug: Choose up to five courses on UCAS. Most deadlines fall in late January; Oxford, Cambridge and medicine close in mid-October.
Write a personal statement and arrange a school reference.
Meet your offer conditions. Some universities ask for a foundation year after 12 years of schooling.
Accept the offer, pay the deposit and receive your CAS.
Hold your funds for 28 days, take the TB test, apply online and give biometrics at the visa centre.
Decisions usually arrive in about three weeks.
pg: Apply directly on university portals 6–9 months ahead; places are filled on a rolling basis.
Prepare bachelor's transcripts, a statement of purpose, two references and a CV. IELTS 6.5 is the common requirement.
Apply for Chevening, Commonwealth or GREAT scholarships; most close between October and December.
Pay the deposit to get your CAS. Some universities hold a short credibility interview first.
Hold funds for 28 days, then apply for the visa and attend biometrics.

sch.t: Strong options for master's students; very little for bachelor's beyond partial university discounts of £1,000–5,000.
list: Fully funded one-year master's for future leaders with two years of work experience. Applications run from August to early November.
Fully funded master's and PhD study for citizens of Commonwealth countries. Most routes close between October and December.
At least £10,000 towards a one-year master's at participating universities, for selected countries. Apply to the university.
Full cost of postgraduate study at the University of Cambridge. Deadline in December or January depending on the course.

name: Canada
pitch: Post-graduation work permits of up to three years and a direct line to permanent residence, though permits are now capped and harder to get.
alerts: Proof of funds rose to CAD 23,448 for applications from 1 September 2026.
A national cap on study permits continues. Most applicants need a provincial attestation letter (PAL); master's and doctoral students at public universities are exempt in 2026.
visa: Study permit

ielts.note: No band below 6.0 is the usual rule for degree programs.

funds.amt: CAD 23,448 for living costs (one person, outside Quebec) plus first-year tuition and travel
funds.how: A GIC from a Canadian bank, plus bank statements, an education loan, or proof that tuition is paid.
funds.held: IRCC asks for four months of bank statements. A GIC has no holding period because the money already sits in Canada.
funds.solv: Officers follow the money trail. Explain every large recent deposit with a sale deed, gift deed or loan papers, and add your sponsor's income and tax documents.

work.term: 24 hours a week off campus in term time, full-time in scheduled breaks.
work.post: Post-graduation work permit of up to 3 years; college programs must be in an eligible field.

spouse.t: A spouse gets an open work permit only if you study a master's of 16 months or longer, a doctorate, or a listed professional program. Spouses of bachelor's and diploma students can come as visitors but cannot work.

unis: Among the lowest fees in Canada
cities: Ocean technology, energy, healthcare and campus jobs.
Agribusiness, aerospace, transport and bank back offices.
Mining, agri-tech and public-sector employers; retail and care work for students.
subjects: Early childhood education and skilled trades

housing.tip: Apply for residence when you accept your offer. Off campus, ask for a written lease and never pay more than first and last month's rent up front.

docs: Letter of acceptance from a designated learning institution (DLI)
Provincial or territorial attestation letter, unless exempt
GIC certificate
Immigration medical exam from a panel physician
Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) if you will study in Quebec
Letter of explanation setting out your study plan
ug: Pick DLIs whose programs qualify for a post-graduation work permit.
Apply on the university portal, or through OUAC for Ontario and EducationPlannerBC for British Columbia.
Accept the offer, pay the deposit and request your attestation letter.
Open a GIC and complete the medical exam.
Apply online to IRCC and give biometrics.
Carry your approval letter and proof of funds to the port of entry, where the permit is printed.
pg: For thesis degrees, find a supervisor and funding first; for course-based degrees, apply on the portal.
Prepare a four-year bachelor's degree (or equivalent), statement of purpose, references, CV and IELTS 6.5.
Receive the admission letter. Public-university master's and PhD students do not need an attestation letter in 2026.
Arrange your GIC and funds evidence.
Apply for the study permit; your spouse can apply for an open work permit if your program runs 16 months or more.

sch.t: Thesis-based master's and PhD students are often funded by their department. Bachelor's students rely on university entrance awards, which are competitive.
list: The government's list of awards open to international students, searchable by country of origin.
Four years of tuition, books and residence at the University of Toronto for bachelor's students. Your school nominates you, usually by November.
Need- and merit-based bachelor's awards at the University of British Columbia. Apply with your admission application by 1 December.

name: Australia
pitch: Family can come with you, partners can work, and regional campuses add extra time on the post-study visa.
alerts: The visa charge rose to AUD 2,500 on 1 July 2026 and is not refunded if the visa is refused.
You must answer Genuine Student questions in the application; generic answers are a common reason for refusal.
visa: Student visa (subclass 500)

ielts.note: The visa itself needs IELTS 6.0, or 5.5 with an English course first.

fee: AUD 2,500 visa charge + Overseas Student Health Cover

funds.amt: AUD 29,710 for 12 months of living costs, plus first-year tuition and about AUD 2,000 for travel
funds.how: Money on deposit with a financial institution, an education loan, a scholarship, or proof of a parent's or partner's annual income above the Home Affairs threshold.
funds.held: No single legal minimum, but case officers and most universities expect deposits to be about three months old or to have a documented source.
funds.solv: Funds can be held by you, parents, a spouse, grandparents or siblings. Show the source: salary, business income, a property sale or a bank loan.

work.term: 48 hours a fortnight in term time, unlimited in breaks. Research master's and PhD students have no cap.
work.post: Temporary Graduate visa (485): 2 years after a bachelor's or coursework master's, 3 after a research degree. Age limit 35.

spouse.t: Your partner and children can be included in your application or join later. Partners can work 48 hours a fortnight, or without limit if you study a master's or PhD. Add roughly AUD 10,400 a year for a partner.

cities: Health and aged care, defence manufacturing and hospitality; counts as regional for visa purposes.
Construction, hospitality and public services, with strong demand for workers.

housing.tip: Use purpose-built student housing or a homestay for the first month, then inspect shared houses in person. Bonds must be lodged with the state authority.

docs: Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
Genuine Student answers in the online form
Overseas Student Health Cover policy for the whole stay
Health examination from a panel clinic
English test taken within the past two years
ug: Choose a CRICOS-registered course and provider.
Apply directly or through a registered education agent. Some universities ask for a foundation year.
Pass the university's Genuine Student screening, then pay the deposit and health cover to receive your CoE.
Lodge the visa in ImmiAccount with your financial evidence.
Complete biometrics and the health examination.
Arrive up to 90 days before the course starts and tell your provider your address.
pg: Check that your bachelor's degree is recognised and whether work experience can earn credit.
For research degrees, secure a supervisor and apply for a Research Training Program scholarship.
Apply for an Australia Awards scholarship if your country is eligible (opens around February).
Receive the offer, pay the deposit and health cover, and get the CoE.
Lodge the visa; include your partner now if they plan to come.
links: Fair Work – your rights at work

sch.t: Full government scholarships exist for eligible developing countries and for research degrees. Coursework students mostly receive university discounts of 10–30%.
list: Full tuition, flights and a living allowance for citizens of eligible countries. Applications usually open from 1 February to 30 April.
Tuition offset and a stipend for research master's and PhD students. Apply through the university you want to join.
Up to AUD 15,000 a year for study at regional campuses. Apply through participating universities.

name: Germany
pitch: No tuition at most public universities, more than 2,000 English-taught master's programs, and an 18-month permit to find work afterwards.
alerts: The blocked-account amount is reviewed each year. It is €11,904 for 2026; check the 2027 figure before you transfer.
Embassy appointment queues in South Asia can run for months. Book as soon as you apply to universities.
visa: National visa for study, then a residence permit

ielts.note: English-taught bachelor's programs are few. Most need German at C1.

tuition.ug: None at most public universities; €150–350 semester fee. Baden-Württemberg charges €1,500 a semester and TU Munich charges non-EU fees.
tuition.pg: Same as bachelor's; a few English master's charge €1,500–6,000 a semester

funds.amt: €11,904 for the first year (€992 a month) in a blocked account
funds.how: A blocked account (Sperrkonto) with Expatrio, Fintiba, Coracle or a bank. Alternatives are a scholarship or a formal obligation letter from a resident of Germany.
funds.held: No waiting period. The account must be funded before your visa appointment and then releases €992 a month after you arrive.
funds.solv: The blocked account is the proof, so a separate solvency certificate is not usually needed. Some embassies still ask for the sponsor's statement to see where the money came from.

work.term: 140 full days or 280 half days a year, roughly 20 hours a week.
work.post: 18-month permit to look for work, then an EU Blue Card.

spouse.t: A family-reunion visa is possible if your stay is longer than a year and you can show enough income and living space. Spouses usually need basic German (A1). It is more realistic for master's and PhD students.

unis: No tuition; most programs in English
cities: DHL's air hub, BMW and Porsche plants and IT working-student jobs.
Automotive suppliers and paid research-assistant (HiWi) posts at the university.
Mechanical engineering firms, logistics and university assistant jobs.

housing.tip: Apply to the local Studierendenwerk for a hall room the day you get your admission letter; waiting lists are long. Shared flats (WGs) are the usual alternative.

docs: Blocked-account confirmation
uni-assist result or preliminary review (VPD) if the university uses it
APS certificate (applicants from India, China and Vietnam)
Health insurance: travel cover for entry, then public insurance on enrolment
Motivation letter and proof of German or English level
ug: Check whether your school certificate gives direct entry in the DAAD or anabin database. Many 12-year certificates need a one-year Studienkolleg or a year or two of university study at home.
Reach German B1 for Studienkolleg or C1 for the degree itself.
Apply through uni-assist or directly. Deadlines are usually 15 July for winter and 15 January for summer.
After admission, open the blocked account and arrange insurance.
Apply for the national visa at the embassy.
Register your address and collect the residence permit after arrival.
pg: Search the DAAD database of international programs.
Check that your credits and grades match; many programs want the German equivalent of 2.5 or better.
Apply through uni-assist or directly. Winter deadlines often fall between 31 May and 15 July.
Open the blocked account.
Apply for the national visa.
Enrol, register your address and apply for the residence permit.

sch.t: With no tuition at most public universities, scholarships here pay living costs. They are mainly for master's and PhD students with strong grades.
list: Monthly stipends of about €992 for master's and €1,300 for PhD, plus insurance and travel. Deadlines vary by program, often between August and November.
€300 a month for at least two semesters, awarded by your German university once you are enrolled.
Stipends for master's and PhD students who are socially and politically engaged. Good German is usually expected. Deadlines 1 March and 1 September.
Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: France
pitch: Public-university fees are set by the state, more than 1,700 programs are taught in English, and master's graduates get a year to find work.
alerts: From 1 August 2026 the living-cost proof rose from €615 to about €877.50 a month.
For 2026–27 almost all new non-EU students pay the full differentiated fee, and non-EU students without a scholarship are reported to have lost housing benefit (APL).
visa: Long-stay student visa (VLS-TS)

ielts.note: French-taught courses need B2 French (DELF or TCF).

tuition.pg: €3,941 a year at public universities; business and engineering schools €8,000–20,000

living: €800–1,200 a month outside Paris; €1,300–1,800 in Paris
fee: €50 through Études en France (€99 otherwise) + Campus France fee

funds.amt: About €877.50 a month, roughly €10,530 for a year
funds.how: Bank statements, a guarantor's letter with their statements, a scholarship certificate, or a blocked account.
funds.held: No formal holding period. Consulates want three months of statements with a stable balance.
funds.solv: A sponsor signs an attestation de prise en charge and attaches ID, bank statements and proof of income.

work.term: 964 hours a year, about 20 a week.
work.post: 12-month job-search permit after a master's or professional bachelor's.

spouse.t: There is no dependant visa on the student route. A spouse applies separately for a long-stay visitor visa with their own funds, or through family reunification once you have 18 months of residence and enough income.

cities: Retail head offices, logistics, hospitality and English tutoring.
Semiconductor firms and research labs, plus seasonal ski-resort work.
Airbus and the aerospace supply chain, and IT services.

housing.tip: Apply for a CROUS hall as early as you can. Private landlords ask for a guarantor; the free state guarantee Visale can stand in for one.

docs: Études en France attestation and Campus France interview certificate
Proof of accommodation for the first three months
Birth certificate with a French translation
Online validation of the visa within three months of arrival
ug: Create an Études en France account if your country uses that procedure; first-year public bachelor's applications (DAP) run from October to mid-December.
Hold French B2, or choose an English-taught bachelor's, most of which are at private schools.
Attend the Campus France interview.
Receive your acceptance.
Apply for the visa at the consulate or visa centre.
Validate the VLS-TS online within three months of arriving.
pg: Search the Campus France catalogue for programs taught in English.
Apply through Études en France (up to seven choices), Mon Master, or directly to the school.
Attend the Campus France interview.
Ask your university to nominate you for the Eiffel scholarship; the deadline is in January.
Apply for the visa, then validate it online after arrival.

sch.t: Government and embassy scholarships cover master's and PhD students; bachelor's funding is rare.
list: About €1,200 a month plus travel and insurance for master's students. Your French university applies for you, with a deadline in early January.
Campus France's searchable list of every French government, embassy, regional and university scholarship.
Awarded by the French embassy in your country; ask its cultural service for the yearly call.
Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: Netherlands
pitch: Hundreds of English-taught degrees, and your university handles the visa paperwork with the immigration service for you.
alerts: You must pass at least half of your credits every year or the university reports you to the immigration service.
Student housing is short. Several universities tell students not to travel without a confirmed room.
visa: MVV entry visa and residence permit, filed by your university
lang: Dutch; most programs for international students in English

funds.amt: About €1,130–1,180 a month in 2026 (roughly €13,600–14,200 a year). The IND resets the figure every January and your university confirms the exact amount.
funds.how: Most students transfer the year's living money to the university, which pays it back after arrival. A bank statement or sponsor declaration in the IND format also works.
funds.held: No holding period when you transfer the money to the university. Bank statements must be recent.
funds.solv: The university is your recognised sponsor and checks your finances itself, so follow its deadline, often 1 June or 1 July.

work.term: 16 hours a week, or full-time in June, July and August. Your employer must get a work permit (TWV).
work.post: Orientation year: 12 months to find work.

spouse.t: A partner can apply as a family member, but you must show stable long-term income, which few students have. It is realistic mainly with a funded PhD or once you start working.

cities: High-tech start-ups around the university, logistics and delivery work.
Energy and IT firms, with a large student job market in hospitality.
ASML, Philips and the semiconductor supply chain.

housing.tip: Register with the student housing provider your university names on the day you accept your offer, and be ready to pay a deposit quickly.

docs: Antecedents certificate (IND form)
Tuberculosis test declaration for listed nationalities
Proof that living costs were transferred
Legalised birth certificate for municipal registration
ug: Check how your diploma compares on the Nuffic website.
Apply through Studielink and the university portal. Non-EU deadlines are often 1 April or 1 May; selective programs close on 15 January.
Accept the conditional offer, then pay tuition and transfer the living costs.
The university files your visa and residence-permit application.
Collect the MVV sticker at the embassy.
Register at the town hall and take the TB test after arrival.
pg: Choose between research-university and applied-sciences master's degrees.
Apply through Studielink and the portal with a GPA around 75% and IELTS 6.5.
Apply for the NL Scholarship and university excellence scholarships, usually by 1 February.
Pay tuition and transfer living costs so the university can file with the IND.
Collect the MVV, travel and register.

sch.t: Scholarships are partial for most students. Full awards are few and go to applicants with top grades.
list: A one-off €5,000 in the first year for non-EEA bachelor's and master's students. Apply through your university, usually by 1 February or 1 May.
€3,000–22,000 for one year of a master's. Apply after admission, by 1 February or 1 May.
Lists the excellence scholarships offered by each Dutch university.
Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: Ireland
pitch: English-speaking, home to the European offices of the big technology and pharma firms, and two years of post-study work after a master's.
alerts: Your course must be on the official list of eligible programs (ILEP), which is being replaced by the TrustEd Ireland mark.
Most visa-required students must pay fees before applying and give biometrics at a visa centre.
visa: Long-stay D study visa, then Stamp 2 permission

funds.amt: €10,000 a year for living costs, plus tuition
funds.how: Bank statements in your name or your sponsor's, plus the receipt for fees paid to the college.
funds.held: Six months of statements are requested, and every large recent lodgement must be explained.
funds.solv: Say who your sponsor is and how you are related, and show their income with payslips, tax returns or business accounts. You must also show access to €10,000 for each later year.

work.term: 20 hours a week in term; 40 hours from June to September and 15 December to 15 January.
work.post: Stamp 1G: 12 months after an honours bachelor's, 24 months after a master's.

spouse.t: Students generally have no right to family reunification. A spouse must apply in their own right, and approval is uncommon for bachelor's or taught master's students. PhD students have a better chance.

cities: Pharmaceutical plants, Apple's European base and tech support centres.

housing.tip: Rooms are scarce in every city. Start three months ahead, use college accommodation offices, and never pay a deposit by bank transfer for a room you have not seen.

docs: Receipt for tuition fees paid
Private medical insurance
Written explanation of any gaps in your education
Details of any previous visa refusals
Signed AVATS application summary
ug: Apply directly to the college; non-EU students do not use the CAO system.
Meet the entry grades. Some colleges ask for a foundation year.
Accept the offer and pay the fees the visa rules require.
Complete the AVATS online form, then submit documents and biometrics at the visa centre.
Register for your residence permit within 90 days of arrival.
pg: Apply directly to each university; most master's degrees last one year.
Prepare transcripts, a statement of purpose, references and IELTS 6.5.
Apply for the Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship (a €10,000 stipend and fee waiver).
Pay fees and apply through AVATS.
Register for your residence permit after arrival.

sch.t: One national scholarship for master's and PhD students, plus university merit discounts of €2,000–5,000.
list: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship
A €10,000 stipend and a full fee waiver for one year of master's or PhD study. Applications usually close in March.
Fully funded one-year master's for early-career professionals from eligible countries. Applications open in summer.
Education in Ireland lists each university's international scholarships.
Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: New Zealand
pitch: A lower funds requirement than Australia, 25 hours of work a week, and a post-study work visa of up to three years.
alerts: Work hours rose from 20 to 25 a week on 3 November 2025.
A partner can work only if you study at master's or PhD level, or a Green List qualification at level 7 or 8.
visa: Fee Paying Student Visa

tuition.pg: NZD 28,000–45,000 a year; PhD students pay domestic fees

fee: About NZD 750; confirm the current fee with Immigration New Zealand

funds.amt: NZD 20,000 a year for living costs, plus tuition and a return airfare
funds.how: Bank statements, fixed deposits, an education loan, or a sponsor's financial undertaking form.
funds.held: Immigration wants to see money held for a reasonable time or a clear source. Three to six months of history is the usual expectation.
funds.solv: Sponsors are normally close family. Show where the money came from: income, savings history, a property sale or a bank loan.

work.term: 25 hours a week in term, full-time in holidays. Research master's and PhD students have no cap.
work.post: Post Study Work Visa of up to 3 years for bachelor's degrees and above.

spouse.t: Your partner can get an open work visa if you study a master's or PhD, or a level 7–8 qualification on the Green List. Other partners can only visit.

cities: Agri-food research institutes, logistics and campus jobs.
Dairy and agri-tech firms, healthcare and retail.
Construction, engineering, tourism and a growing tech sector.

housing.tip: University halls include meals and suit the first year. For flats, pay bonds only through Tenancy Services.

docs: Offer of place
Tuition receipt, or payment after approval in principle
Medical certificate and chest X-ray
Police certificate if you will stay 24 months or longer
Travel and medical insurance
ug: Choose from the eight universities or a polytechnic; some courses ask for a foundation year.
Apply directly to the institution.
Receive your offer of place.
Apply online to Immigration New Zealand at least three months ahead.
After approval in principle, pay your fees to receive the eVisa.
pg: Pick a postgraduate diploma, a taught master's or a research master's.
For research degrees, agree a topic with a supervisor first.
Apply for the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship if your country is eligible.
Receive the offer and apply for the visa.
Your partner can apply for a work visa alongside you.

sch.t: A full government scholarship for eligible countries, and domestic-level fees for every international PhD student.
list: Full tuition, living allowance and flights for citizens of eligible countries. Applications usually open in February.
International Student Excellence awards of up to NZD 10,000 for bachelor's and master's students.
International excellence awards of up to NZD 15,000 towards tuition.

name: Italy
pitch: Income-based tuition that can fall below €1,000 a year, and regional scholarships that pay for fees, meals and a living allowance.
alerts: The proof of funds rose to €10,179.85 a year for 2026–27, up from €6,947.
Visa applications for 2026–27 bachelor's and master's enrolment close on 30 November 2026.
visa: National D study visa after Universitaly pre-enrolment

ielts.note: Many universities accept a medium-of-instruction letter instead.

tuition.ug: €500–4,000 a year at public universities, based on family income

funds.amt: €10,179.85 a year, about €848 a month
funds.how: A personal bank statement stamped by the bank. Scholarships count; cash, crypto and property do not.

tuition.pg: Free in Czech; €2,000–8,000 a year in English; medicine €12,000–16,000

funds.amt: About CZK 125,000 for a one-year stay; the formula is tied to the subsistence minimum and housing costs
funds.how: A bank statement in your name together with a payment card for that account, or a funding commitment from a state body or legal entity.
funds.held: The balance must be available on the statement date. A long history is not required, but the account must be yours.
funds.solv: A private sponsor's letter alone is not accepted; the money has to be in your own account.

work.term: No hour limit and no permit for full-time students in accredited degree programs.
work.post: 9-month permit to look for work; graduates have free access to the labour market.

spouse.t: A spouse can apply for a long-term visa for family reasons with proof of funds, housing and insurance. Processing is slow, so apply early.

unis: Czech University of Life Sciences Prague
cities: IT companies, shared-service centres and very low unemployment.
Tourism, multinational service centres and English teaching.

housing.tip: University dormitories (koleje) cost CZK 4,000–7,000 a month and come with the accommodation form the visa needs.

Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: Portugal
pitch: Mild climate, moderate fees and living costs, and a year to look for work after graduation.
alerts: The funds benchmark follows the minimum wage, which is €920 a month in 2026.
The immigration agency AIMA has long backlogs; book your residence appointment as soon as you arrive.
visa: D4 study visa, then an AIMA residence permit
lang: Portuguese; growing number of English master's

ielts.note: Most bachelor's degrees need B2 Portuguese.

funds.amt: €920 a month, about €11,040 for 12 months; less if housing or meals are already paid
funds.how: Bank statements, a scholarship, or a term of responsibility signed by a sponsor resident in Portugal.
funds.held: Consulates ask for three to six months of statements.
funds.solv: Add 50% of the benchmark for each extra adult and 30% for each child.

work.term: 20 hours a week in term, full-time in breaks.
work.post: 12-month stay to look for work.

spouse.t: Residence-permit holders can apply for family reunification with extra funds, but 2025 law changes added waiting periods for some categories and queues are long. Check the current rule before you plan around it.

unis: Among the lowest fees in Portugal
cities: Software and electronics firms, textiles and call centres.
Health and biotechnology, tutoring and hospitality.
Technology hubs, tourism and multilingual customer support.

housing.tip: University residences are cheap but few. Book a private room before the September rush and keep the contract for your residence permit.

For Portuguese language and culture studies and for citizens of partner countries.
Fee reductions for the best-ranked international students.
Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: Japan
pitch: National-university tuition of about ¥540,000 a year, generous MEXT scholarships, and 28 hours of part-time work a week.
alerts: Your school applies for the Certificate of Eligibility four to five months before the intake, so deadlines are early.
Some national universities have raised tuition above the standard ¥535,800.
visa: Student visa, issued after a Certificate of Eligibility
lang: Japanese; English-taught degrees at about 80 universities

ielts.note: Japanese-taught courses need JLPT N2 and the EJU exam.

tuition.ug: ¥535,800 a year at national universities, plus a one-off ¥282,000 admission fee; private ¥800,000–1,500,000
tuition.pg: ¥535,800 a year at national universities; private ¥700,000–1,400,000

funds.amt: No single legal figure. Immigration looks for roughly ¥2 million, about a year of tuition and living costs, through your sponsor's records.
funds.how: The sponsor's bank balance certificate, copies of bank books and income and tax certificates covering up to three years, and a signed letter of financial support.
funds.held: Schools commonly ask how the balance was built up over one to three years, not only for a current figure.
funds.solv: A formal bank balance (solvency) certificate carries real weight here, and it must match the income documents.

work.term: 28 hours a week with a work permission stamp, and up to 8 hours a day in long vacations.
work.post: Job-hunting status for 6 months, renewable once.

spouse.t: Your spouse and children can get Dependent status if you show you can support them. Dependants may work 28 hours a week with permission.

cities: Start-ups, shops and restaurants, and logistics, with lower rents than Tokyo.

housing.tip: University dormitories are cheapest. Private flats ask for key money and a guarantor, so share houses are simpler for the first year.

list: Tuition, about ¥117,000–145,000 a month and flights. Apply through the Japanese embassy in April–May, or through a Japanese university in autumn.
¥48,000 a month for self-financed students; your Japanese school nominates you after enrolment.
Full funding for master's study at partner universities, for citizens of Asian Development Bank member countries with work experience.
Fully funded master's for young government officials from selected countries.

name: South Korea
pitch: Strong engineering and technology universities, the fully funded Global Korea Scholarship, and work hours that grow with your Korean level.
alerts: Part-time hours depend on your TOPIK level; without it the limits are much lower.
Dependant visas for students' families were restricted in 2025.
visa: D-2 student visa
lang: Korean; about 30% of courses in English at major universities

ielts.note: TOPIK 3–4 is accepted instead for Korean-taught courses.

tuition.pg: ₩5–10 million a year national; ₩8–16 million private

funds.amt: A bank balance of ₩20 million for universities in the Seoul area or ₩16 million elsewhere; many schools quote US$20,000
funds.how: A bank balance certificate in your name or your parents', issued within the past 30 days. A scholarship certificate reduces the amount.
funds.held: Many embassies and universities want the balance kept for three to six months, some only one. Your admission guide states the rule.
funds.solv: Add a family-relation certificate if the account is your parents'. Applicants from some countries face stricter document checks.

work.post: D-10 job-seeker visa, extendable to as long as 3 years.

spouse.t: F-3 dependant visas were restricted in 2025. In practice only master's and PhD students with enough funds qualify, and F-3 holders cannot work.

cities: Port logistics, shipbuilding, tourism and cafés.
Car plants, an AI cluster and the food industry.

housing.tip: Take the dormitory for the first semester. Private rooms need a large deposit, so many students choose a goshiwon or one-room with a small deposit.

list: Tuition, about ₩1 million a month, flights and a year of Korean language. Bachelor's applications run September–October, graduate ones February–March, through the embassy or a university.
Fully funded master's for government officials and public-sector staff from partner countries.
Full tuition and a monthly allowance for most admitted international students.

name: China
pitch: Low tuition, very large government scholarship schemes, and English-taught medical and engineering degrees.
alerts: Part-time work needs approval from both your university and the immigration office, and the hours are tightly limited.
Most universities require international students to live on campus in the first year.
visa: X1 visa, then a residence permit

ielts.note: Chinese-taught courses need HSK 4–5.

funds.amt: No national minimum. Universities usually ask for proof of about US$5,000–10,000, or a scholarship shown on the JW201/JW202 form.
funds.how: A bank statement or deposit certificate, or a government or provincial scholarship letter.
funds.held: Usually a recent statement; some universities ask for a deposit frozen for three to six months.
funds.solv: The university sets the rule, so follow its financial-guarantee form exactly.

work.term: Only with university and immigration approval; typically no more than about 8 hours a week in term.
work.post: Limited. Some cities allow master's graduates to apply for a work permit directly.

spouse.t: Your spouse and children can apply for S1 long-stay visas as family of an X1 holder, with marriage and birth certificates. They cannot work.

cities: Optics and electric-vehicle industries, with approved campus jobs.

housing.tip: International dormitories on campus cost ¥600–1,500 a month. If you move off campus, register your address with the police within 24 hours.

list: Tuition, a dorm place, medical insurance and ¥2,500–3,500 a month. Apply through the Chinese embassy or directly through a university, usually January to April.
For Chinese language study and teaching degrees. Apply through a Confucius Institute or partner school.
The agency that runs the national scheme; its site lists participating universities.

name: Malaysia
pitch: English-taught degrees at a fraction of Western prices, including branch campuses of British and Australian universities.
alerts: Students may work only during semester breaks, in a few sectors, with Immigration approval.
Your university submits the visa application to EMGS; you cannot apply on your own.
visa: Student Pass through EMGS
intakes: Several a year: January–March, May–July, September–October

ielts.note: Requirements vary by subject; health sciences need more.

tuition.ug: MYR 8,000–20,000 a year at public universities; MYR 20,000–45,000 at private and branch campuses
tuition.pg: MYR 8,000–25,000 a year public; MYR 20,000–50,000 private

fee: About MYR 1,000–2,000 for EMGS processing, medical screening and insurance

funds.amt: No published national figure. Universities ask for evidence that you can cover first-year fees and living costs, commonly US$4,000–6,000 plus fees.
funds.how: A bank statement or sponsor letter submitted with the EMGS application; some nationalities also sign a personal bond.
funds.held: Usually the last three months of statements.
funds.solv: The university decides what it accepts before it submits your file.

work.term: No work in term time. Up to 20 hours a week in breaks longer than seven days, in restaurants, petrol stations, mini-markets and hotels.
work.post: A 12-month Graduate Pass exists for selected nationalities; otherwise you need an Employment Pass.

spouse.t: Master's and PhD students can bring a spouse, children and parents on dependant passes arranged through EMGS. They cannot work. This is not open to most bachelor's students.

cities: Internships at multinational service centres; part-time work is limited.
Manufacturing and data centres, next to Singapore.

housing.tip: Campus hostels are cheapest. Off campus, rent a room in a shared apartment near a train line and ask for a stamped tenancy agreement.

Master's scholarships for citizens of partner developing countries.
Graduate research assistantships and fee waivers.

name: Singapore
pitch: Two universities in the world's top 20 and Asia's financial hub on the doorstep, at a high cost and with no family route.
alerts: The Tuition Grant cuts public-university fees sharply in return for working three years in Singapore after graduation.
Students at most private schools are not allowed to work.

intakes: August (public universities); private schools all year

tuition.ug: S$17,000–40,000 a year with the Tuition Grant; private schools S$15,000–30,000

funds.how: A bank statement or sponsor letter if the school or immigration authority asks; a security deposit or banker's guarantee for some nationalities.
funds.held: Recent statements; the immigration authority can ask for more.
funds.solv: Public universities rarely ask for bank papers, but private schools often do.

work.post: A one-year Long-Term Visit Pass for graduates of public universities to look for work.

spouse.t: Student's Pass holders cannot sponsor a spouse. A visiting spouse uses a short-term visit pass.

Close to NUS, with research-assistant and tutoring work.
Cheaper rooms, with logistics and retail employers.

Full PhD funding with a monthly stipend. Two intakes a year.
Merit scholarships for bachelor's students, considered with your admission application.

name: United Arab Emirates
pitch: Branch campuses of British, Australian and American universities, with the visa sponsored by the university itself.
alerts: Your school certificates must be attested and declared equivalent by the Ministry of Education.

funds.held: Usually the last three to six months of statements.
funds.solv: The university is your visa sponsor, so its checklist is the one that counts.

work.post: Golden Visa for top graduates; others move to an employer-sponsored visa.

Hospitality, events, property and fintech internships.

Full scholarship, housing and stipend for every admitted master's and PhD student in artificial intelligence.
PhD scholarships and merit discounts for strong bachelor's students.

name: Türkiye
pitch: The lowest total cost on this list, with the Türkiye Bursları scholarship covering tuition, a stipend, housing and flights.

tuition.pg: US$300–3,000 a year public; US$4,000–12,000 private

funds.held: Usually a statement covering the last three months.
funds.solv: The residence-permit office in your city may ask for the proof again after you arrive.

work.post: No automatic stay. An employer must sponsor a work permit.

spouse.t: Family residence permits generally require the sponsor to have lived in Türkiye for at least a year with sufficient income. Spouses often enter on their own short-term permit.

Student cities with aviation and manufacturing employers.
Tourism, trade and export offices that need foreign-language staff.

housing.tip: State dormitories are very cheap but limited for international students. Private dorms and shared flats near campus are the usual choice.

Monthly stipends for international master's and PhD students in science and engineering.
Full scholarships (tuition, travel and about €1,400 a month) for two-year master's taught across several European universities. Apply to each program's consortium, mostly between October and January.

name: Malta

name: Romania
pitch: EU degrees from about €2,000 a year, some of the lowest living costs in the Union, and medical degrees taught in English and French.
alerts: You first need a Letter of Acceptance issued by the Ministry of Education. Your university applies for it, and it can take one to two months.

visa: Long-stay study visa (D/SD), then a residence permit

name: Estonia
pitch: Europe's most digital society: no limit on student work hours, nine months to find a job afterwards, and a start-up scene that hires in English.
alerts: The income requirement rose to €880 a month in 2026.
Estonia has few embassies, so many applicants must travel to another country for the visa interview. Check where yours is before you apply.
visa: Long-stay D visa, then a temporary residence permit for study

ielts.note: The University of Tartu asks for 6.0 and 6.5.

tuition.pg: €2,000–7,500 a year; many master's have tuition-waiver places

funds.amt: €880 a month of legal income in 2026, so €10,560 for a year
funds.how: Bank statements, scholarship letters, or proof of regular income from you or a supporter. Any third party may support you, not only family.
funds.held: No holding period. Proof of regular income is accepted as readily as a balance, but you must be able to document where it comes from.
funds.solv: You confirm the income when you sign the application, and the case officer can ask for the papers at any time.

work.term: No hour limit, as long as you keep studying full-time and pass your courses.
work.post: You may stay 270 days after your permit ends to look for work.

spouse.t: A bachelor's or master's student must usually have lived in Estonia for two years on a residence permit before a spouse can apply to join them. Doctoral students are not subject to that wait.

cities: University spin-offs, software firms and research labs.
Technology companies, start-ups and customer-support centres working in English.

housing.tip: University dormitories cost €120–350 a month; apply as soon as you are admitted. Private rooms in Tallinn are scarce in August.

list: The official list of state and university scholarships for degree students.

Full or partial waivers on selected master's programs, decided at admission.

name: Latvia
pitch: Affordable EU degrees in English, a state scholarship for eligible countries, and Riga's growing business-services sector.
alerts: The subsistence requirement rose to €780 a month from 1 April 2026.
State scholarships are open only to citizens of the countries on the official list; check it before you count on one.
visa: Long-stay D visa or a temporary residence permit for study
fee: About €60–120, depending on the visa or permit route

funds.amt: €780 a month, so about €9,360 for a year
funds.how: A bank statement in your name, or a sponsor's statement with a guarantee. Some missions also ask for a debit or credit card that works in euros.
funds.held: No holding period is published; a recent statement showing the full amount is the norm.
funds.solv: Universities quote the yearly total they want to see, so use your admission letter's figure if it is higher.

work.term: 20 hours a week in term and 40 in holidays. Master's and doctoral students may work 40 hours a week.
work.post: Master's and doctoral graduates can request a 9-month permit to look for work.

spouse.t: A spouse can apply for a residence permit if you show the extra subsistence (the adult rate again, plus a smaller amount per child), housing and insurance. It is assessed case by case.

unis: Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies
cities: Shared-service centres, IT firms, aviation and hospitality.
Food processing, engineering and campus jobs, 40 minutes from Riga.
Manufacturing and the lowest rents in the country.

housing.tip: Student hostels cost €100–250 a month. Most private flats are advertised on one classifieds site, so check it daily in August.

name: Lithuania
pitch: Low fees, a fintech and business-services job market in Vilnius, and a full year to look for work after you graduate.
alerts: From 22 May 2026, first- and second-year bachelor's students may work only 20 hours a week; later years and master's students may work 40.
Your previous qualification must be recognised before admission, and parliament has been tightening residence and family rules for non-EU students. Check the Migration Department before you apply.
visa: National D visa or a temporary residence permit for study

funds.amt: €577 a month for 12 months plus €1,153 for the journey home: about €8,077
funds.how: A bank statement in your name, a scholarship letter, or a sponsor's statement with a notarised guarantee.
funds.held: The balance must cover the whole amount on the statement date; no holding period is published.
funds.solv: The monthly figure is half the national minimum wage, so it changes every January.

work.term: 20 hours a week in the first two bachelor's years; 40 hours from the third year and for master's students. No separate work permit.
work.post: 12-month permit to look for work or start a business.

spouse.t: Family reunification normally requires two years of residence, with exceptions for some categories. Draft rules would stop master's students bringing family at all, so confirm the current position with the Migration Department.

cities: Manufacturing, IT and logistics, with a large student population.
Fintech firms and international shared-service centres.

housing.tip: University dormitories cost €100–250 a month; apply the day you are admitted. For private flats, expect one month's deposit.

name: Greece
pitch: Low living costs for the eurozone, new English-taught degrees at public universities, and year-round tourism work.
alerts: Sources disagree on the funds figure: the long-standing legal minimum is €400 a month, but universities and consulates now commonly ask for €500–700. Use the number your consulate gives you.
Most public bachelor's degrees are taught in Greek; English-taught ones are still few.
visa: National D visa for studies, then a residence permit
lang: Greek; a growing number of programs in English

ielts.note: Many master's programs accept 6.0.

tuition.ug: €1,500–9,000 a year for English-taught degrees; medicine about €12,000

funds.amt: Commonly €500–700 a month (about €6,000–8,400 a year); the legal minimum has long been €400 a month
funds.how: A bank statement, a scholarship letter, or a sponsor's declaration with their statements.
funds.held: No holding period is published; consulates usually ask for the last three to six months of statements.
funds.solv: You must show the funds again each time you renew the residence permit.

work.term: Part-time, up to 20 hours a week.
work.post: A one-year permit to look for work exists under the 2023 migration code; confirm the procedure with the regional immigration office.

spouse.t: Family reunification generally requires two years of lawful residence and proof of stable income, so a spouse usually cannot join during a short degree.

unis: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
cities: Tourism, the port and multilingual call centres.
Research institutes, agriculture and seasonal tourism.
Shipping companies, tourism and multilingual customer-support centres.

housing.tip: University halls are limited for international students, so most rent a studio or share a flat. Sign a contract registered on the tax portal; you need it for the residence permit.
